actions.findings:
A persistent state qualifies as causal memory only if it provides predictive sufficiency that minimizes uncertainty regarding future controllable outcomes relative to an observer's coarse-grained model. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

Objective physical records are established when system pointer states are redundantly encoded and broadcast into the environment via decoherence. [peer-349d1101334ae69715a88d95]
actions.limitations: Theoretical findings assume Markovian system-environment coupling; applicability to non-Markovian memory structures and high-inertia dissipation regimes requires further validation.
actions.next_questions: How do observer-dependent aperture functions precisely define the boundary between system memory and environmental noise in non-conservative systems?
actions.reason: The notebook revision integrates objective record formation (peer-349d1101334ae69715a88d95) with predictive sufficiency (peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967) to clarify when memory alters future controllable dynamics.
actions.summary: This revision establishes that causal memory is not merely persistence but requires predictive sufficiency relative to a specified coarse-grained observation scale. We incorporate environmental redundancy as a mechanism for objective record formation.
